subject: CFA  models parameters and Satorra-Bentler adjustment

messages.author: 7ade812063b4a211
messages.subject: CFA  models parameters and Satorra-Bentler adjustment
parts:
Dear all,

I am very new in using lavaan.  My question is related to CFA  models parameters. It is not a real lavaan question but I thought of trying maybe someone can help.

Trying to run CFA, I found that many parameters can be use to assess models fit.
CFI, TLI which should be close to 0.9 for good fit
RMSEA should be <= 0.05 for good fit

My models showed good values of CFI and TLI but RMSEA models are greater than 0.10.

I read that non-normality of data sets might be the cause of poor model fit.

I found that a solution is to adjust data with Satorra-Bentler scale. But it did not change my models parameters.

My question is:
- Between the different parameters of CFA models which one is the best to assess model fit?
- Any idea why adjusting with Satorra-Bentler the parameters did not change?

For a little context,, we are investigating the perception of nature landscapes by people living in Azores.

I can provide more details if it can help.

Many thanks,

Noelline

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: CFA models parameters and Satorra-Bentler adjustment
parts:
Noelline,
It is important to distinguish model parameters (like factor loadings, effect coefficients and variances) from fit indices (like CFA, TLA and RMSEA).  (There is a further distinction that can be made between indices with no known distribution (like CFA and TLS) and fit statistics with known distributions, like RMSEA) but this distinction is not as fundamental or generally recognized.)

There are different perspectives in the literature on how best to evaluate fit.  However, one common view is that it is not a good idea to rely on any one fit index (or statistic) to tell the whole story.  It is important to evaluate parameter estimates, model residuals, and a profile of summary statistics in making judgments about model fit. You can find a detailed discussion of assessing model fit in Rex Kline's SEM text.

I am not sure whether your second question refers to parameters or fit indices.  See the "estimator" section of the lavOptions help file for a description of what is and is not affected by the adjustment.  The most direct way to confirm that you have successfully requested the adjustment might be to directly compare the model chi-square values.

Keith
